figures.finding: Bermuda has no rule of its own for child performers: the Employment of Children and Young Persons Act reaches 'any employment whatsoever', so a child under thirteen may not be employed at all (save light family farm, garden or domestic work for a parent-employer, or light carrying by hand), with no exception for acting; a child or young person below the upper compulsory school age may not work in school hours or more than two hours on a school day; no one under eighteen may work at night (20:00 to 06:00), save to midnight from sixteen. No permit, licence or chaperone rule exists, and the Act draws no line between performing, writing or directing.

value.under13Exception: light agricultural, horticultural or domestic work where the parent or guardian is the employer; light transport by hand
value.night: 20:00-06:00 barred under 18; to midnight allowed from 16

figures.finding: A minor (under eighteen) is bound by the common law of minors' contracts, which the Minors Act saves; the Act makes void a minor's contracts for money lent or goods other than necessaries and bars suing on a promise to pay after full age. No statute provides for a court's approval of a minor's engagement or sets any share of a minor's earnings aside, and none distinguishes performing from writing or directing.

value.void: loans and goods other than necessaries (s. 23)
value.binding: common law (s. 3 saves rights and liabilities arising by operation of law)

sources.said: “minor” means a person who has not attained the age of eighteen years; … Except as otherwise provided in this Act, nothing in this Act shall be construed so as to affect any right or liability arising by operation of law out of the relations between any person and a minor. … All contracts, whether under seal or by way of simple contract, entered into by minors for the repayment of money lent or to be lent, or for goods supplied or to be supplied (other than contracts for necessaries), and all accounts stated with minors, shall be absolutely void:

figures.finding: The Companies Act sets no minimum age for a director: a company is managed by at least one director elected by the members, and the Act's only bar on taking part in management is undischarged bankruptcy; a minor's capacity to bind himself as a member or director rests on the common law of minors' contracts.
